_about.fields: Match, Severity (blocker: do not convert this machine for this program; friction: an alternative exists but is not a drop-in; info: worth knowing), Note, Source, Verified

Risks.Note: Adobe Creative Cloud does not run on Linux and Adobe has stated it will not. Alternatives (GIMP, Krita, Inkscape, DaVinci Resolve, Kdenlive) are capable but are not drop-in replacements, and none open .psd/.ai files with full fidelity. If you are paid to use these, do not convert this machine.

Desktop Office does not run on Linux. Office on the web works fine in a browser, and LibreOffice or OnlyOffice handle most documents - but complex Excel macros and heavily formatted Word files will break.
Accounting and tax software is Windows-only and rarely has a usable Linux equivalent. If you run a business on this, keep a Windows machine or a Windows VM.
Professional CAD/EDA/GIS software is Windows-only. FreeCAD, KiCad and QGIS exist and are good, but file compatibility with commercial formats is imperfect.
Kernel-level anti-cheat blocks Linux by design. These specific games will not run, no matter what you do. Most other games work well through Steam Proton - check protondb.com for your library.
Steam runs natively on Linux and Proton makes most Windows games work. Check protondb.com for your specific library before committing.
No Linux iTunes. iPhone sync and backup is limited; Apple Music works in a browser.
No official Linux OneDrive client. Third-party sync clients exist and work, but setup is manual.
Visual Studio (the full IDE) is Windows-only. VS Code, JetBrains Rider and the .NET SDK all run natively on Linux.
